title: Lemma A: a current on ℝ^P vanishing off a compact K ⊆ U has M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U)
statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ U compact, and Z ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ q) with Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Let Z|_U := Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) ∈ D_q(U), so Z|_U(ω) = Z(ω) for ω ∈ D^q(U) ⊆ D^q(ℝ^P). Then M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U), where M(Z) = Z.mass = Z.massOn univ and M(Z|_U) = (Z|_U).mass = (Z|_U).massOn U.
lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → Z.mass ≤ (Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).mass
